Stage 1 finished with 25 rows after applying the drop rule. Now I need to score the predictions and build the results table, then check whether the remaining context budget allows running Stage 2 with HF, since that's expensive per channel.

Checking PN1 against the s/d frontier rows with a relaxed 0.08 tie threshold: K, Ca, Rb, and Sr all fail the tie condition with gaps around 0.09-0.14, while Sc, Y, Cs, Ba, La, Fr, Ra, Ac, Lu, Hf, Rf, and Th all hold with gaps under 0.08. So roughly 13 of 17 rows satisfy PN1, with the failures clustering around the alkali/alkaline earth entrants.

For the p-block control check, Ga's 4p channel sits much shallower than the swapped 4s channel by about 0.27, but since there are no empty partner channels at Ga the control condition is technically vacuous as originally stated — though the depth gap itself still confirms the p electron is the most weakly bound.

Checking where 4f starts collapsing to become the deepest channel, I find it holds at Z=57, 58, 64, 89-92, and 96, but fails at 55, 56, 87, and 88. That pattern shows the f-collapse only kicks in once a d-electron is present to screen it — the La-type onset — not at the preceding alkali/alkaline earth rows, and this holds even under the relaxed criterion at 57, 58, and 64.
